title: Do Elections Matter to the Stock Market? | Dimensional
gist: Promo page for Episode 60 of Dimensional's Informed Investor podcast arguing that election outcomes show no strong link to stock market performance, and that investors overweight home-market politics while ignoring politics abroad.

insights.claim: Dimensional says the data shows no strong connection between election results and stock market performance, so election outcomes are a weak basis for portfolio changes.
insights.speaker: Featuring Mark Gochnour, Head of Global Client Services Group
insights.so_what: Avoid repositioning portfolios around election results; treat election-driven trades with skepticism.
insights.quote: The data doesn’t show any strong connection between election results and stock market performance.

insights.claim: Investors tend to overemphasize the impact of elections in their home market while ignoring politics in other countries, a home-bias in how political risk is perceived.
insights.speaker: Featuring Mark Gochnour, Head of Global Client Services Group
insights.so_what: Political risk attention is unevenly allocated; diversification across countries is not driven only by domestic politics.
insights.quote: Investors may overemphasize the impact of elections in their home market while ignoring politics in other countries.

insights.claim: The episode frames common beliefs about elections moving markets as myths to be interrogated with evidence ahead of the election.
insights.speaker: Featuring Mark Gochnour, Head of Global Client Services Group
insights.so_what: Expect Dimensional's election-season messaging to counsel staying invested over timing.
insights.quote: We interrogate common myths about the impact of elections on markets

source_meta.author: Featuring Mark Gochnour, Head of Global Client Services Group
